body.text:
Docs refresh is done and committed (`035bcd7`):

**README** is now a human-focused project page: it opens with what git-for-ai *is for* — "source control that remembers why" — and the two convictions driving it (agents should record more than a diff; humans must be able to review what their agents did). Then a what-works-today command table, a quick start, the privacy defaults, and a documentation map. All the "how this repo came to be" narrative — the Rust→TypeScript pivot story, the founding decisions, process notes — moved to `architecture/history/PROJECT_GENESIS.md`.

**History has a home**: `architecture/history/` now holds the genesis doc plus the two archived session notes (the 2026-07-17 handoff and the end-of-day resume note). The repo root and `architecture/` proper contain only living documents.

**Plans are current**: CLI_PLAN.md marks M9/M10 ✅ with their commits and points at PLAN_2026-07-18.md as the authoritative ordering; PLAN_2026-07-18.md carries a progress banner (W1 complete, `report` shipped early, M11 in progress). One honest note in that banner: the `config` command is the only W1 stub still outstanding — it's small and I'll fold it in alongside M12's wiring.

The M11 query-engine agent is still working in the background. When it lands: verify, commit, then M12 gives you `git for-ai ask` and `blame --why` — and the README's "in progress" line gets shorter again.

The plan's answer has two layers, because we deliberately reframed the desktop app when you sharpened the vision two days ago.

**The original framing** (MONOREPO_PLAN) was thin: an Electron + React shell around the same `core` engine, "for people who want `blame --why` and `ask` as a GUI, not a terminal command." Essentially: the CLI's query features with pixels. It also fixed two structural decisions that still stand — the desktop app calls `core` in-process (Electron's main process is just Node, so no local HTTP hop), and it shares its React components with the future website so nothing gets built twice.

**The current plan** (PLAN_2026-07-18 §2.2, which you approved) recenters it on *agent-activity review* — the "prove it to me" surface — with four core functions, in priority order:

1. **Timeline** — commits × agents × changes, filterable by day, agent, and model. The "what did my agents do this week" view.
2. **Change detail** — the diff side-by-side with the ledger entry: summary, intent, rejected alternatives, constraints, with `confidence` / `scope_risk` / `reversibility` rendered as visible flags, and the *evidence* right next to the claims — the `tested` entries alongside the session spans showing those tests actually running.
3. **Session trace viewer** — the captured spans as a readable narrative (what the agent ran, what it edited, what failed and got retried), not raw JSON.
4. **Attention queue** — the review-worthy items surfaced automatically: `doctor` findings, low-confidence entries, `inferred`/orphan identities. Browsing is for everything; this is the "look at these first" inbox.

Plus, once M12 lands, the **ask panel** — semantic search and "why is this line like this?" navigation — which is the only part genuinely blocked on the query engine.

**The delivery path matters as much as the features**: the plan explicitly says don't start with Electron. First comes `git for-ai review` — a local web app the CLI serves, reading through `core` in-process, no network, no accounts. The Electron `desktop/` package then becomes a thin wrapper around that same React app, built only "once the SPA has proven what a GUI should be." You've already seen the seed of all this: `report.html` is the static prototype of exactly this information design — the review SPA is that page made live, filterable, and eventually askable.

Worth being honest about what's *not* specified yet: no mockups, no interaction design, no decision on things like diff rendering or how deep session-trace navigation goes — the plan deliberately keeps the desktop at direction-level detail until the SPA exists and real usage shows what matters. That's the same don't-design-against-imagined-usage principle that kept the server small.

Good instinct to check — the honest answer is: it's in the **plan** as an approved direction (PLAN_2026-07-18 §2.2: the four functions, SPA-before-Electron, served by the CLI), but it is **not yet in the architecture** as a buildable spec. Nothing pins the package layout, how the CLI actually serves it, the data contracts, or the security posture. Every milestone so far has been built against a written spec, and that discipline has paid off repeatedly — so I'll write the spec first (it's compact, since §2.2 and the existing structured data shapes do most of the work), then launch the build. Writing it now:

attributes.command:
cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add architecture/REVIEW_UI.md && git commit -q -m "Add REVIEW_UI.md: buildable spec for the local review web app

The plan's §2.2 direction made concrete: packages/review-ui (Vite+React
SPA, no core imports, shared later by desktop/website), served by a new
\`git for-ai review\` command over node:http — 127.0.0.1 only, read-only
GET API wrapping the already-tested runReport/runShow structured
results, zero external requests, non-minting reads. v1 scope: timeline,
change detail (reasoning-first; diffs are v2), session trace narrative,
minimal attention queue, disabled ask panel until M12.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1
